stream_identity.epoch_rule: A restored, replaced, or incompatible observation projection creates a new opaque epoch whose first sequence is 1.
stream_identity.sequence_rule: ProjectionSequence is positive, unique, contiguous, and commit-ordered within one ObservationStreamEpoch.
stream_identity.cross_epoch_rule: Sequences from different epochs are never numerically compared.

snapshot_contract.consistency: Item heads, time head, gap state, stream epoch, and ThroughSequence are read in one repeatable committed view.
snapshot_contract.resume: A client applies only events from the same epoch with ProjectionSequence greater than ThroughSequence.
snapshot_contract.empty: An empty snapshot still returns epoch, ThroughSequence, time, and explicit NO_SAMPLE states.
snapshot_contract.bounded: Item count, encoded bytes, source-epoch count, and query filters are bounded server-side.

event_types.delivery: one immutable sample identity plus current-head revision
one durable freshness transition with policy revision and evaluated time
expected and observed source sequence bounds without synthesizing samples
one durable read-only alarm projection transition
one typed time observation with source, provenance, and uncertainty
liveness and server time only; never advances ProjectionSequence
terminal stream frame with reason, authoritative epoch, and authoritative sequence

delivery_rules: Subscribe before replay so a racing commit is read durably, observed as a wake-up, or both and then deduplicated.
Live fan-out is only a wake-up signal; every delivered data event is reread from the committed observation outbox.
Events are deduplicated by EventId and ProjectionSequence and delivered in increasing contiguous sequence.
Telemetry may be batched or coalesced only when individual sample identities remain queryable and dropped count, source-sequence bounds, and gap facts are explicit.
Freshness, gap, alarm, epoch, and resynchronization transitions are never silently coalesced.
Keepalive, browser time, and connection state never establish telemetry freshness or advance a cursor.

cursor_outcomes.action: send stream.resync_required without comparing sequence values and close
deliver the durable gap event; conditions remain indeterminate until a new complete snapshot

backpressure.slow_consumer: close with CLIENT_QUEUE_OVERFLOW and require a new snapshot
backpressure.priority: observation traffic cannot consume or reorder the v0.4 lifecycle stream queue or cursor

reconnect_restart: Reconnect with a same-epoch available cursor replays exactly the committed suffix and then continues live.
Reconnect with an unavailable or different-epoch cursor requires a complete replacement snapshot.
Backend restart resumes relay from unpublished committed observation events and collector reads from durable per-item source cursors.
Driver source restart creates a new SourceEpoch and visible source transition without resetting the observation projection epoch.
Projection restore or incompatible rebuild creates a new ObservationStreamEpoch and never offsets an old cursor.
cancellation_shutdown: Client disconnect cancels its bounded queue subscription and no driver GetTM NEXT request.
Collector shutdown cancels outstanding driver NEXT calls, commits no partial sample, and retains the last durable source cursor.
Server shutdown closes authenticated streams without manufacturing a cursor advance.
security_rules: Snapshot and stream require authenticated authorization and expire with credentials.
Filtering and redaction occur before cursor allocation for an authorization scope; hidden events cannot leak count or timing.
Query-string credentials are forbidden; the approved WebSocket subprotocol carries the bounded token.
Event payloads contain no secrets, raw peer diagnostics, host paths, or unapproved catalog values.
